On the certificate-of-disposition request, the field census's effectiveLabel for a vertical stack of identifier fields on page 2 is the label of the row above, not the row it is attached to, while labelBasis still claims printed_to_the_left_in_the_same_cell. Two anchors are correct and each is followed by a run of shifted labels, which is the signature of a label-picking rule that mis-resolves in a dense stack. FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: The repair added a well-drafted section that names a checkable authority, and it still fails, because it asserts a silence the repository does not have. The section states: "No held source establishes what it costs to file a CPL 160.59 sealing application", that neither application source states a filing fee, states that filing is free, or describes a fee waiver, and that the packet "does not supply a figure it does not hold" — then names the clerk's office of the court of conviction and sentencing as the office to ask. The claim about the two forms is correct and this lane confirmed it independently: extracting the text of both the application and the pro se packet from the mounted corpus finds no fee, cost or dollar figure anywhere on either face. But the claim about the repository is false. The compiled New York profile, cited as a requiredSourceId for this exact route, answers it directly: packetGenerator.feeRules[2] reads "CPL 160.59 sealing application — No separate filing fee — Court motion; notarization needed", and the profile's narrative repeats it — "the 160.59 motion itself carries no separate filing fee" — and its agent guidance says to note that the motion has no separate filing fee. Amendment A1 settles the ordering: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer, and a named checkable authority may stand in only where none does. One does here, so the stand-in is unavailable and the packet sends the participant to ask a question the repository already answers. The packet's third paragraph shows it can do this correctly — it states the certificate-of-disposition fee, $5 outside New York City and $10 in the five boroughs, sourced to the form's own face, and the compiled profile's feeRules[0] and [1] hold exactly those figures. The repair is to state the no-separate-filing-fee answer the profile holds alongside the certificate fee it already states, and to carry across the waiver-adjacent facts the profile also holds — that legal-aid organisations and county district attorney sealing units assist pro se applicants at no cost.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Passes on A3's per-fact test, and the pass is unusually well evidenced. Naming the fact and the route: the court filing fee for a Utah criminal expungement petition under 77-40a-305. Finding the record that establishes that fact for that route: the district court cover sheet 1044XX, which is a bound component of this very packet and which prints '$150 [ ] Expungement Petition - Criminal (E)' on its page 2. The packet states '$150', names the form and page it comes from, and — the part that makes it checkable — selects that row on the delivered artifact, which I confirmed on raster/boundary/page-07.png. On the waiver the packet is better than most: it names Utah court form 1305GE, the Motion to Waive Fees for Expungement – Criminal, under Utah Code 78A-2-302 and Rule 4-508, says plainly that the form is not included in this fixture and where to get it, and rehashes to the 1305GE in the corpus. SERVICE.detail: Two committed records answer this route's service question and they answer it in opposite directions. I can prove the conflict; I cannot resolve it, and a verifier who picked a side here would be doing counsel's job. What the packet says: 'The prosecutor must receive a copy of what you file, by mail or by email', attributed to BCI's Expungement Applicant Instructions, with the packet's form 1146XX, Acceptance of Service – Expungement (Prosecutor), offered for the prosecutor to acknowledge receipt. That attribution is accurate and I verified it from the source bytes — the BCI instructions I rehashed to 9e03980f… head their Step 2 'File the petition with the court and serve the Prosecutor' and carry the line 'Mail or email the prosecutor copies of what you file'. What the committed track registry says, in the entry for track ut_pet_acquittal itself: rules.service reads 'The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case: the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The Proof of Service form appears in the published packet only as an optional form, used where the prosecutor's office will not accept service.' It goes further and warns against the very wiring the packet has made: 'The Utah Courts general service-of-process page governs first papers in a new civil case and must not be wired to this track; doing so would import a summons, a process server and a 120-day deadline this track does not have.' rules.notice says the same from the other side: 'The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney.' And the national route-obligation census carries it in the destination detail for both of this route's keys: 'The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.' So the packet states, as a requirement, a step that two route-keyed committed records say the petitioner does not have. This is not the A3 case — A3 settles what to do when a record is off-point, and here both records are on-point for this exact route — so A3 does not break the tie and I am not going to invent a rule that does.
SERVICE.whyNotScoredAsAFailure: Because I cannot show the packet is wrong. The BCI instructions are the issuing agency's own applicant instructions for Utah expungement, they are held in the corpus, they rehash exactly, and they say what the packet says. It is entirely possible that both are true in practice — the court transmits the filing and BCI advises the petitioner to send copies as well — in which case the packet is merely belt-and-braces and the registry's 'does not serve' is about legal obligation rather than practice. It is also possible the registry is right and the packet imposes a step on a participant that Utah does not require, which is a real cost in effort and a possible source of confusion about the 1146XX form's status. Deciding which needs someone who can read Chapter 40a and URCrP 42 against BCI's page, and that is counsel.
SERVICE.whyNotScoredAsAPass: Because the prior lane failed this obligation citing the registry sentence the packet now contradicts, and passing it silently would bury a conflict the factory has already noticed once. It would also let a family reach a terminal verdict on a participant-facing direction that a committed record denies.
SERVICE.theQuestionForCounsel: On the ut_pet_acquittal route, must the petitioner mail or email the prosecutor a copy of what is filed, as BCI's Expungement Applicant Instructions direct, or does the court transmit the filing to the prosecuting attorney with no service obligation on the petitioner, as the committed track registry and the route census both state? If both are true, which should the packet tell the participant to do, and what is form 1146XX's status — a required acceptance of service, or the optional fallback the registry describes for where a prosecutor's office will not accept service?
SERVICE.whatIsNotInDoubt: The rest of the section is sound whichever way the answer falls. SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: Stated, on the standard these four lanes have applied. The packet's first line frames what it is — 'a review fixture built from exact held official Utah forms' — and 'What this packet is not' states the three sentences the passing families in these lanes state: 'It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the court will grant expungement.' It goes beyond a disclaimer in two places that matter. It names a reachable human authority, the Utah State Courts Self-Help Center on 888-583-0009, in the same breath as the event most likely to need one: 'The prosecutor or a victim in your case may object; if the court schedules a hearing, attend it.' And it draws a boundary around its own knowledge rather than only around its legal status, telling the participant which facts it will not guess and why, and instructing them to ask BCI what the certificates cost rather than assuming. That is the construction on which vt_seal_felony-set and rcap-oh-custom-pleading-clean-tracks were passed in these lanes.
SELF_HELP_STOP.advisory: One held stop condition is missing and it is the strongest one in the registry. The committed track registry lists eight selfHelpStopConditions for this track and marks the first as a hard stop in its own words: 'The participant is not a US citizen. The Utah Courts self-help page itself tells non-citizens to consult an immigration lawyer before expunging, because the FBI may retain records of an expunged case. This is a hard stop, not a caveat.' The packet does not carry it. Of the other seven, the objection-and-hearing condition is addressed in substance and the public-interest-showing condition is partly addressed by requiring the participant to write their own explanation; the remaining five — a BCI special certificate instead of a certificate of eligibility, conviction-counting near the 77-40a-303(4) and (5) limits, an active protective order or stalking injunction, appellate records, and a not-guilty-by-reason-of-insanity verdict — are not carried. I record this rather than failing on it, for the same reason as on my Kentucky and Pennsylvania rows: A1 and A2 confine the establish-then-state ordering to FILING_DESTINATION, FEE_AND_WAIVER and SERVICE, and extending it to SELF_HELP_STOP is a Captain's decision that would move many families at once. But this instance is the sharpest I have seen, because the registry does not merely list the condition — it labels it a hard stop and gives the reason, and the packet is silent on it. If a Captain acts on my cross-family flag anywhere, this is the family to act on first.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: A clipped run of the official form's own text on the delivered primary filing, present in all four variants, in a family no central visual gate has ever looked at. I found it by measurement and then confirmed it by eye. Running a word-geometry read with pdftotext -bbox over all sixteen delivered fixtures isolates it exactly: the twelve unchanged-official documents have zero words outside the page box, and all four cr-409-filled.pdf fixtures have one, on page 2. The word is 'otection' at x0 -3.442, running off the left edge of the 612-point page. Comparing against the build's own derived source shows what happened. In derived-sources/cr-409-pikepdf-unlocked.pdf the form's viewer notice is set as two lines: 'For your protection and privacy, please press the Clear' at y 756.9 starting at x 36.0, and 'This Form button after you have printed the form.' at y 766.5. In the filled artifact those two lines have been re-flowed into a single line at y 765.1, which is about 74 points too wide for the page, and the overflow has run off the left-hand side — so 'For your pr' is gone and the line begins mid-word. On raster/pc-851-91-matter-of-right-boundary/cr-409/page-02.png it reads 'd privacy, please press the Clear This Form button after you' truncated at the paper's edge and running underneath the green 'Print this form' button. So it is both clipped and overlapping. I am scoring it against the same standard I applied to ny_160_59_petition-set in my other lane, where a word-geometry read plus a raster read established a clipped write and the obligation failed.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.severityStatedPlainly: Lower than New York's, and a Captain should weigh it as such. What is clipped here is the form's own viewer chrome — the notice telling a user to press the Clear This Form button after printing — not a participant's name, address or email, and not a substantive line of the filing. Nobody's petition is wrong because of it. What it is, is a delivered page with visibly broken text on it in a Grade-A packet, and a fidelity defect against the official form: the notice is intact and correctly placed in the source and mangled in the artifact. The build damaged text it was not writing into.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.whyNothingElseCaughtIt: This family is in RASTER_QUEUE.json's notEligible list rather than its rows, so no central visual gate has ever run on it, and there is no receipt asserting no clipped write. The nine completeness counters read visualDefects 0 because they are not a pixel measurement. The defect sat in every delivered primary filing with nothing positioned to see it.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.repair: The fill and flatten path for CR-409 re-flows a two-line static text run on page 2 into one over-wide line and lets it overflow left. Fix the flatten so static content streams are preserved rather than re-laid-out — the original page content streams are byte-identical between the exact source and the pikepdf-unlocked derivative, per this family's own source-fidelity.json, so the damage is introduced after the unlock and is in the writer, not the source. Re-measure with a word-geometry read afterwards, since no central gate will catch a regression here.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.fleetRelevance: Worth a Captain's attention beyond this family. The cause is a flatten path applied to an encrypted XFA Judicial Council form, and California's packet families are built from that same class of source. If the writer re-flows static runs generally, other California families built the same way will carry the same defect, and none of them can be checked by the central gate for the same page-parser reason that excluded this one.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: A recorded failure, properly repaired, and repaired to the record's own words. The defect was that the packet said the court's address was 'not established in this repository' and sent the participant to the clerk, while the committed packet-set manifest held a two-branch venue rule, a filing deadline and a one-arrest-per-petition limit for this exact packetSetId. All three are now stated. The manifest's file entry reads 'File the verified CR-409 with the proposed CR-410 at least 15 days before the hearing, in the court where the accusatory pleading was filed, or where no pleading was filed in a court with criminal jurisdiction in the city or county where the arrest occurred. One arrest per petition.' The packet's 'Where you file this, and by when' section states that sentence. I compared them directly rather than trusting the section heading. Both venue branches are there — the court where the pleading was filed, and the fallback where none was — along with the 15-day deadline and the one-arrest limit. A1's test is answered in the right order: the repository established it, so the packet states it, and it no longer substitutes a question to the clerk for an answer the record holds. The clerk is still named, but now only for what the record genuinely does not hold — the payment methods and any local intake rule.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Both halves now met, on A3's per-fact test set out in full in feeStandardAmendmentsApplied above. The fee half was already right and remains right: no held record establishes an amount for an 851.91 petition — the compiled profile's on-point line says 'Arrest sealing (851.91) Filing fee varies County Superior Court' and the manifest's pay_fee entry says 'Unresolved and county-specific. Do not publish a figure.' — so the packet publishes none, quotes the manifest's wording, explains that publishing an amount it does not hold would be worse than publishing none, and names the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of the arrest, which is the same office the profile itself names. The waiver half was the recorded defect and is repaired. The earlier finding was that the packet said whether a fee can be waived is 'not established in this repository' while the manifest's apply_fee_waiver entry names FW-001, and that the string FW-001 appeared nowhere in the family directory. It appears twice now, and the treatment is careful in a way that respects A3: it names FW-001 as the general California fee waiver form, says plainly that it is a separate form not included in this packet and not filled in, says where to get it, and then declines to assert what the record does not establish — 'whether a waiver is available on this particular petition, and what it requires of you, is decided on your own financial circumstances and on that court's practice'. Naming a held general form without claiming it necessarily applies to this route is exactly the distinction A3 asks for.

SERVICE.detail: The most consequential of the three recorded failures and the best-repaired. The defect was that the packet said who must be served and by what method were 'not established in this repository' and sent the participant to the clerk — while shipping CR-106, the Judicial Council's own proof of service, with all 33 of its blanks mapped. The earlier finding put it exactly right: the participant had the instrument for proving service, had been told the parties were unknown, and had a 15-day deadline nobody mentioned. All of that is now stated. The manifest's serve_party entry reads 'Serve the prosecuting attorney of the city or county where the arrest occurred, and the arresting agency, at least 15 days before the hearing', and the packet's 'Who you must serve, and by when' section states that sentence. Two named recipients and the deadline. The packet then does two things the finding did not ask for and that make the section work. It explains why CR-106 is in the packet at all — 'it is the proof that you served those parties' — which closes the gap between having the form and knowing its purpose. And it states the ordering rule and the direction the clock runs: 'Serve first, then complete the proof of service — never the other way round. The deadline runs backwards from the hearing, so count from the hearing date, not from the day you file.' A participant who reads that cannot make the two mistakes this route invites.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: Stated, and given a section of its own rather than left to a closing line — this family is the only one of my seven with a heading that says 'Where this packet's self-help ends'. The section does three distinct things. It bounds the packet's knowledge: it states what the repository holds for this route and nothing beyond it, and names the filing fee, the payment methods and any local intake rule as things that come from the clerk rather than from the packet. It bounds the packet's role: it does not decide whether the arrest qualifies to be sealed, it does not appear for the participant, and it is not legal advice. And it names two trigger conditions with an instruction attached, which is what separates a stop from a disclaimer: 'If your case does not match the route named at the top of this page, or if anyone opposes the petition, that is the point to get a lawyer or a legal-aid office rather than to press on with these papers.' Opposition is the right trigger to name for 851.91, because an opposed petition is where the interests-of-justice branch turns into an argument. The first line of the packet also states its own status honestly — these are deterministic review fixtures made from exact held official sources and are not approved filing packets — which is the sentence on which an earlier VF02 row passed this obligation for this family, and it is now the least of the reasons to pass it.

decisiveDefect.heading: ## The filing fee
decisiveDefect.theSentence: Neither the petition nor the order states a filing fee, and no source this packet holds establishes what filing this petition costs — or whether it costs anything.
decisiveDefect.whyItIsWrong: The second clause is a claim about the repository and the repository answers it. src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/AR-arkansas.json states it three times, read in this lane at this base: line 2506 'Sealing petition filing fee $0 Filing fees eliminated by the 2019 amendments'; line 2505 'Act 1460 eliminated sealing filing fees; the real costs are records and any counsel'; and line 2484, in the filing rule, 'File in the circuit or district court that handled the case. Act 1460 eliminated filing fees for sealing.' The same profile's form table at line 2444 places 'Petition and Order to Seal Misdemeanor DWI / BWI Driving- or boating-while-intoxicated misdemeanor; 10-year wait' among the Act 1460 uniform petition-and-order pairs, so the fee elimination reaches THIS route and not merely a sibling — DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A3 is satisfied on the route, not stretched across one.
decisiveDefect.theProofItIsReachable: The sibling ar-arrest-seal-set, built from the same profile in the same state under the same Act, states it: 'There is no filing fee for this petition… the compiled Arkansas profile… states it three ways'. One route in this state publishes the held answer and this one denies the answer exists.

It also refuses the cross-read explicitly: 'Do not assume the court's $150 waiver covers any BCI amount — the court and BCI are two different offices with two different waivers.'

SERVICE.detail: The registry records that the court transmits to the prosecutor and the petitioner does not serve. FEE_AND_WAIVER.evidence: This family is the waiver route, and it states the fee position with unusual care. It records that art. 102.006 was repealed effective 2025-09-01 and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01, that under 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee applicable to an ex parte petition in a civil action rather than a fixed sum, and that a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100 under (b). It refuses to reproduce the $250-to-$500 figure that circulates online, naming it as coming from the repealed statute. It gives the two places the fee is waived without this form at all, art. 102.0061(c) and (d), with the articles to cite at the counter. And it states the art. 55A.254(f) $25-per-paper-agency transmission charge, that it lands twice, and that ten paper-only agencies costs $500 -- more than the fee being waived. Rule 145's requirement that the clerk supply this form free and without being asked is stated twice.

SERVICE.evidence: Stated, and correctly inverted from what a participant would assume. Under 'WHO SERVES WHOM - AND IT IS NOT YOU' the packet says the clerk sends the petition and the notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax; that the court sets a hearing not earlier than the thirtieth day after filing and gives a copy to each official, agency or entity listed other than central federal depositories; and that DPS notifies those itself, so the filer does not chase the FBI. That is the registry's service and notice rules for these tracks, faithfully, including its 'The participant does not serve in the ordinary case'. It adds the practical half: build the agency list from the clerk's published art. 55A.253(c) list, use the e-mail addresses, deduplicate, and note that a state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service.

SELF_HELP_STOP.evidence: Stated, on the composed page and again in the instructions, under 'When to stop and get help instead'. pageEightRuling.question: FIX42 names a residual five-line page 8 at SCAN01's fragment threshold and asks VF04 to rule: is a five-line page carrying prose plus the trailer a visible defect on a delivered page?
pageEightRuling.ruling: NO. Page 8 is thin, not defective.
pageEightRuling.inOneSentence: Page 8 of 14 is thin but not defective: its own words are a whole, self-contained participant-facing disclosure -- 'Two of the findings in that sentence - good moral character, and rehabilitation to the court's satisfaction - are the court's to make. They are not facts LegalEase can supply and nothing in this packet asserts them.' -- closed by the same route footer that closes every composed component in this packet, with nothing clipped, split, overlapped, or placed in a court-owned block.
pageEightRuling.whatIsOnThePage: Five drawn lines: two of prose at y=720.0 and y=705.5, and the three-line route trailer at y=691.0, 676.5 and 662.0, all at 11pt from x=72.0. The lower 83 per cent of the page is blank.
pageEightRuling.whyThatIsNotTheDefectVF03Failed: VF03 failed pages 8 and 13 because every line on them was a machine route identifier: a page whose entire delivered content is an internal artifact gives the reader nothing, and that is a defect. What page 8 now delivers is a complete legal disclosure that begins and ends on this page, telling the participant that two of the statutory findings are the court's to make and that the packet asserts neither. A reader turning to page 8 meets no broken word, no truncated line, no identifier without context and no ink where it does not belong.
pageEightRuling.whySparsenessIsNotItselfADefect: SCAN01's five-line fragment threshold is a screening heuristic on line count. The obligation is measured on what is visible on a delivered page, and a low line count is not a visible defect; a page that ends a component early is an ordinary pagination outcome. Page 13 of the same fixture is the same shape with three lines of prose and is the same answer.
pageEightRuling.theOneThingWorthFixingAndWhyItIsNotAFail: The trailer sits 14.5pt below the prose on page 8 -- one line pitch, no blank line -- where every trailer elsewhere in this packet has 29pt above it. The pull-down consumed the paragraph break. It is a spacing inconsistency in the shared block paginator at scripts/build-census-v1-ri_decriminalized-set.mjs, visible but not illegible and outside every class the CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP standard names. It is recorded as an observation for the host owner, not as a failed obligation, and it does not hold this verdict.

sharedToolingFinding.title: Whole-file SHA-256 pins on shared national records go stale whenever any other jurisdiction is amended
sharedToolingFinding.scope: cross-family, not specific to any family this cohort read
sharedToolingFinding.measured: Every source-receipt.json under data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1 was scanned at base 5de917b3574b6e27df362e13b86b4bfaac4915f8 and every pinned repository record recomputed with sha256. 233 receipts; 45 pins; 35 recompute equal; 10 are stale, spread over 10 families.

twoRecordsAccountForAllTen.data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet: 7 stale pins, 0 current. Amended 8 times in the history reachable here; receipts across the census pin 4 different historical digests of it (80d88d69..., 563147bf..., 713ed7ab..., 6076f734...), and only 6076f734... is the file today.
twoRecordsAccountForAllTen.data/rcap-ledger/completed-output-counse: 3 stale pins, 0 current. Pinned at 99e80291... (commit eab70f926); current is fbf9bfef... (commit cb6cbf45e), whose only delta to the file is one added Kansas route entry.

sharedToolingFinding.whyItHappens: Both records are national and are amended in place as each new jurisdiction is productized. A per-family receipt that pins the whole file therefore fails the moment an unrelated state is added, even though the family's own entry is untouched. I confirmed for both families in this cohort that the family's own entry is byte-identical between the pinned commit and this base, so no legal statement moved.
sharedToolingFinding.whyItMatters: SOURCE IDENTITY is stated as an exact recomputation, so a verifier that measures it honestly must fail these families, and a repair lane must re-pin. The re-pin then goes stale again on the next unrelated amendment. Two of this cohort's six FAIL-bearing obligations are this defect and nothing else.
sharedToolingFinding.suggestedDurableFix: Pin the family's own subtree of a shared national record - the packetSetId entry, the route entry - rather than the whole file, or record the pin as {commit, path, selector, subtreeDigest}. Either makes the binding survive amendments to other jurisdictions while still failing if the family's own legal content changes. This is a decision for a tooling or Captain lane; this cohort verifies and does not repair.
sharedToolingFinding.whatThisIsNot: Not a defect in the two records themselves, not a legal-content change, and not grounds to re-render any fixture. Every affected family here is bound by a hash-bound RASTER_PASS receipt to the bytes on disk, and re-rendering would cost it that gate for a receipt-field correction.

The hashes match and pdf-lib parses the files, but no other family in this cohort produces these errors from the same pdf-lib pipeline. Recorded on that family's row and repair assignment.

The RASTER_PASS receipts for all six families name documentsCovered as the canonical assemblies only (both canonicals, for the two-variant ar-drug-court family).
